stories.body: A gunman opened fire in Kraków’s main square on Saturday, killing six people and wounding at least 15, including two police officers, authorities said. Police shot and detained the 25-year-old Polish suspect, whom the interior minister described as fascinated by far-right ideology and holding ultranationalist views. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the attack terrorism and said three more people, apparently members of the suspect’s family, were found dead at his home. Poland declared two days of national mourning.
stories.headline: Six killed in Kraków shooting; three bodies found at suspect’s home

stories.body: President Isaac Herzog has chosen former military chief Gadi Eisenkot to attempt to form Israel’s next government after an election left both his opposition alliance and Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc short of a majority. Eisenkot received recommendations from 67 lawmakers, including members of Arab-led parties, but has ruled out including those parties in a government. He will have 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension, to build a coalition; Netanyahu remains prime minister in the meantime.
stories.headline: Israel’s president picks Gadi Eisenkot to try to form a government

stories.body: Russian attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure and a bridge over the Dnipro left Kyiv facing electricity, water and heating disruptions. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia used 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles in the attack on Kyiv and surrounding regions, and that five people were injured. The strikes came ahead of planned talks in Abu Dhabi between Russian, Ukrainian and US negotiators. Zelenskyy warned against discussing a wider European security framework before Russia ends its war and Ukraine receives meaningful security guarantees.
stories.headline: Russian strikes disrupt Kyiv’s power and water ahead of peace talks

stories.body: At least 30 people were reportedly killed in an attack on a market in Yemen’s Taiz province. The Houthis blamed Saudi airstrikes, while government forces and local authorities accused the Houthis of indiscriminate fire. Separately, Houthi-run media reported that strikes killed at least 27 people in a village in Sanaa province, most of them women and children, and blamed the Saudi-led coalition. Al Jazeera said it could not independently verify the reports; the attacks come amid intensified fighting and widespread displacement.
stories.headline: Deadly attacks in Yemen leave civilians caught between rival claims

stories.body: Prime Minister Christopher Luxon’s National party and its current coalition partners were projected to hold 67 seats in a 130-seat parliament, a one-seat majority, after nearly all ordinary votes were counted. Hundreds of thousands of special votes, including overseas ballots, remain to be counted and could change the result. Neither Luxon nor Labour leader Chris Hipkins claimed victory, and coalition talks could take weeks. Official results are expected on November 27.
stories.headline: New Zealand election remains too close to call

stories.body: A sharp sell-off in US technology stocks spread to Asian and European markets after the Democrats’ midterm victory, as investors weighed the prospect of tighter oversight of AI data centers and questioned returns on heavy spending. The Nasdaq fell 5.5% on Thursday before recovering 1% on Friday; Japan’s Nikkei and South Korea’s Kospi also fell sharply. The debate over data centers extends beyond the US, with activists occupying the site of a planned Microsoft facility in Amsterdam.
stories.headline: AI stocks fall as investors worry about data center growth

stories.body: President Donald Trump has publicly asked UFC chief executive Dana White to become White House press secretary. White said he would meet Trump on Monday to discuss the offer. Trump also named several current and former UFC fighters whom he wanted White to bring as assistants. The press secretary position has been vacant since Katie Zacharia’s five-day tenure ended last month.
stories.headline: Trump offers press secretary job to UFC chief Dana White

stories.body: Democratic governor-elect Gina Hinojosa plans to challenge Texas education policies including school vouchers and state takeovers of school districts. New school officials may also revisit policies that brought religion into classrooms and reduced diversity efforts. Hinojosa says she hopes to win bipartisan support, though some Republican legislators are already seeking to block her agenda before she takes office.
stories.headline: Texas governor-elect plans to reverse Republican education policies

stories.body: Democratic lawmakers say they will focus on the cost of living, investigations into alleged corruption and tighter oversight of immigration enforcement agents as they prepare for divided government.
stories.headline: Democrats set priorities for divided government

stories.body: A general strike planned for Wednesday has grown out of a tenants’ movement protesting the difficulty of accessing housing. The tenants’ union proposed the action, while the major labor unions UGT and CC OO formally called it. Labor minister Yolanda Díaz has encouraged participation, while opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo has urged unions to call it off. In Barcelona, about 450 people demonstrated on Saturday against the rising cost of living, according to city police.
stories.headline: Housing crisis drives plans for November 11 general strike

stories.body: El Hierro’s island government has declared a social emergency after more than 8,000 people arrived by boat in five weeks, putting pressure on reception, health and rescue services. Island officials have asked the Canary Islands government and Madrid for more staff, facilities and coordinated transfers to other islands. The Spanish government has called a meeting for Tuesday with Canary Islands president Fernando Clavijo and El Hierro’s president, Alpidio Armas, to discuss the situation.
stories.headline: El Hierro declares emergency after surge in migrant arrivals

stories.body: Iñaki Barrón, former president of Spain’s railway accident investigation commission, has called for a thorough audit of the high-speed network following the Urda crash. His engineering association estimates that high-speed maintenance needs €10 billion over the next decade. Separately, railway safety agency data show 207 accident precursors, such as track deformation and trains passing signals without authorization, on high-speed lines between 2017 and 2024. Two crashes on the Madrid–Seville line, at Adamuz and Urda, have killed 115 people in nine months.
stories.headline: Rail expert calls for high-speed network audit after Urda crash

stories.body: People’s Party leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo says he wants a large enough majority to govern without coalition partners, but has left open a deal with the far-right Vox party after Spain’s November 29 general election. Polls place his party ahead while suggesting it would need Vox’s support to govern. Feijóo says he would not ask the Socialist Party to abstain to let him take office without Vox.
stories.headline: Feijóo says a coalition with Vox depends on the election result

stories.body: Barcelona’s council has approved the basis for a joint city and Catalan government company to rehabilitate roughly 4,000 homes in Besòs-Maresme, with a proposed budget of €415 million. A financial report considered the possible demolition and replacement of 1,800 homes with severe defects, alarming residents. The city says the report had to examine alternatives and that it is pursuing rehabilitation, not demolition. A neighborhood group is considering asking prosecutors to investigate the handling of earlier regeneration plans.
stories.headline: Barcelona approves public company to rehabilitate Besòs-Maresme homes

stories.body: Renfe says an operational problem involving shortages of drivers and trains has caused cancellations and delays across Rodalies and southern regional services. New work schedules followed the end of an agreement with Semaf, the main drivers’ union, and some drivers have been unable to reach their starting locations normally. The R1, R2 Nord, R2 Sud and R4 have seen delays of 20 to 30 minutes or more. Semaf has also called two strike days for the coming week.
stories.headline: Rodalies and regional trains delayed amid driver and train shortages

stories.body: Catalan police have arrested seven alleged members of a network and 43 business owners accused of arranging fictitious employment contracts to help migrants enter Spain or seek legal status. Investigators say people in Pakistan paid up to €30,000 for visas, documents and contracts, while others already in Spain paid up to €8,000 for contracts to begin regularization. Police say some people never received work and others worked in precarious conditions. Three of those arrested have been jailed.
stories.headline: Police arrest 50 in alleged migrant-entry scheme

stories.body: A historic Tramvia Blau car is on static display on Avinguda del Tibidabo this weekend to mark the tramway’s 125th anniversary. Visitors can board the car, and its workshop will open to the public on November 14 and 15. An exhibition at Diagonal metro station runs throughout November. The tram last operated in 2018, and the city has said the process of restoring service will begin in 2027.
stories.headline: Tramvia Blau returns for a 125th anniversary display
